queue.caption:
LUNARIA, restaurant website design concept 🌕

LUNARIA is a fine-dining concept: six courses cooked over olive wood, served on a terrace that faces the moon.

The name is the moon itself. The site opens the way the night does: a gold ring draws, the moon waxes from crescent to full, and the name comes into focus.

The graphic system is an astrolabe. The plate turns inside an engraved ring of roman numerals, two rings turning against each other, with a wax seal for the six courses.

The palette is midnight and champagne gold, with moonlight only at the edges.

Motion is slow and quiet. The tasting menu is a deck of cards that peel away one course at a time, and every booking ends with a wax seal: "See you on Friday, 21:00."

The result is a website that feels like the dinner before you've booked it.

Role: concept, web design, UI, motion, front-end

Want your restaurant to feel like this online? DM me "FIX".

queue.caption:
Hotel website design review: my own concept failed, so I rebuilt it.

Review & redesign, Ep. 01. I start with my own work.

NOCTILUCA is a design concept: a small hotel built around the night swim. Version 1 looked good and still failed three of my seven questions:

1. Where does the eye land first? Nowhere. The headline, the text and the readout all compete.
2. Does the headline say the offer? "Stay up for the sea" never says hotel.
3. Does every section earn its place? Under the hero sat a brand book: name meaning, mark, colour, type. Guests don't book a font.

Version 2 follows the order a guest decides in: the offer and one button, why this place, the rooms, the stay hour by hour, reviews, then the ask again. And the page follows the sun: 15:00 at the top, 23:00 at the bottom.

Send this to someone whose website looks nice but doesn't get bookings.

Want yours reviewed? DM me "FIX".

#hospitalitymarketing #directbookings #designprocess #webdesigner #uxdesign
